preconditions.description: t is an integer between 1 and 1000 inclusive, representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(n == int(n) and 1 <= n <= 50 for n in [int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and line.split()[0].isdigit()])
preconditions.description: Each test case starts with an integer n between 1 and 50 inclusive, representing the size of the polygon matrix.

preconditions.expression: all(len(matrix) == n and all(len(row) == n and all(c in '01' for c in row) for row in matrix) for matrix in [stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+1+n] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)])
preconditions.description: Each matrix is a square of size n x n, where each cell is either '0' or '1'.

postconditions.expression: all(stdout_line.strip().upper() in ['YES', 'NO'] for stdout_line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is either 'YES' or 'NO' (case-insensitive).

postconditions.expression: all((stdout_line.strip().upper() == 'YES') == (is_possible(matrix) for matrix, stdout_line in zip([stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+1+n] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)], stdout.splitlines())))
postconditions.description: The output 'YES' for a matrix means there exists a sequence of cannon shots that can produce the given matrix. The output 'NO' means no such sequence exists. The function `is_possible(matrix)` is defined as follows: A matrix is possible if and only if for every cell (i, j) with value '1', either (i == 1 and j == 1) or there exists a cell (i, k) with k < j and value '1' (for row cannons) or a cell (k, j) with k < i and value '1' (for column cannons) that blocks the '1' in (i, j). Additionally, no '1' can exist in the first row or column unless it is the only '1' in its row or column, respectively, or is blocked by another '1'.

postconditions.expression: all((stdout_line.strip().upper() == 'NO') == (not is_possible(matrix) for matrix, stdout_line in zip([stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+1+n] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)], stdout.splitlines())))
postconditions.description: The output 'NO' for a matrix means no sequence of cannon shots can produce the given matrix, i.e., the matrix violates the blocking rules for at least one '1'.
